title: where Clause
concept: The where clause moves type constraints after the function signature — keeping complex signatures readable and organized.
why: When you have 3+ type parameters each with multiple constraints, the function signature becomes unreadable. where clauses restore clarity.
syntax_ref:
fn name[T, U](params) -> ReturnType
  where T: Constraint1 + Constraint2,
        U: Constraint3,
{ /* body */ }
tips: Use where when the inline syntax becomes hard to read — about 3+ constraints total
Each where line should be one logical group of constraints
Place where after the return type but before the opening brace
where clauses work with both functions and impl blocks
common_mistakes: Using where for simple signatures with one constraint — unnecessary ceremony
Forgetting the comma between where clauses
Putting where before the return type — it goes after
